Module · Step 3

Currency Translation

Translation runs on the adjusted trial balance. Balances are carried from the recording currency to the functional currency, then from the functional currency to the reporting currency, and the resulting remeasurement gain or loss and translation adjustment are attributed between the parent and non-controlling interests.
Translation engines

Exchange rate master

Rates by type, currency pair and effective date

Average and spot rates drive the period translation. Historical rates carry an identifier so each equity or non-monetary event is translated at the rate that applied on its own date.
{{ fxRmCount }}
{{ h.label }}{{ h.sub }}
{{ r.leg }} {{ r.ident }} {{ r.status }}
{{ fxCalMonth }}
{{ w.label }}
{{ fxCalSelText }}
The identifier is built from the rate type and the period: A for average, SC for spot closing, SO for spot opening and H for historical, followed by the period number on the effective date (1–12 for months, 1–4 for quarters). A3 is therefore the Q3 average. Where two historical events fall in the same period they are suffixed in date order.

Module · Step 4

Intercompany Eliminations (ICE)

Nine elimination natures, one input template. Fill only the natures that apply to the period; the engine matches reciprocals, carries unrealised profit forward and attributes the result to the parent and non-controlling interests.
{{ icFileName }}
{{ icFileMeta }}
One upload supplies every nature at once. Amounts in the transaction currency, positive magnitudes on both sides; the engine derives debits and credits from the elimination type and handles translation.
